transformations.name: De-tensorize
transformations.statement: Replace an invariant that composes badly under products with one that composes correctly.
transformations.diagnostic: Stated in the seed only informally.

seed_evidence.note: On cases 2 and 3 the needed move runs the opposite way: progress required an invariant that is MULTIPLICATIVE, because the target itself is (super)multiplicative. Case 1 changes the product law from additive to Pythagorean.

transformations.name: Collectivize a union bound
transformations.statement: Replace a union bound over m bad events with a single collective argument.
transformations.diagnostic: A union bound over m events appears in the composition slot.

seed_evidence.note: Candidate refinement, UNTESTED: ask whether some instance in the class makes the m bad events near-independent. If it does, the log is real.

transformations.name: Auxiliary-witness lift
transformations.statement: Introduce an auxiliary object whose existence certifies the bound.
transformations.seed_verdict: NO STATED DIAGNOSTIC; NEAR-ZERO DISCRIMINATING POWER

seed_evidence.note: Fits almost anything post hoc. This is the programme's own E9 criticism applied to the programme.
Only case 2 fits, and only weakly - it abolishes the iteration entirely.

candidate_replacements.statement: Compute how the target behaves on the product construction of the extremal family, and require the invariant to obey the same law.
candidate_replacements.relation: E4 becomes the special case where the target is flat.
candidate_replacements.fatal_caveat: Derived from the same cases it was then scored on. It needs cases chosen by someone who has not seen the hypothesis. Until then it is a guess.
